notes: §1985:VI.3.2.1.2 SR1: 'The comment-entry may be any combination of the characters from the computer's character set. The continuation of the comment-entry by the use of the hyphen in the indicator area is not permitted; however, the comment-entry may be contained on one or more lines.' The entry's characters and its several lines conform: CommentEntryOf opens the paragraph at an Area-A word that CommentEntryParagraphs names inside an IDENTIFICATION DIVISION and keeps it open over every following line with no Area-A word, and the lines are discarded before the lexer reads them. The prohibition is asked of the line (kb/Work PB5169): a line of an open comment-entry with a hyphen in the indicator area is COBOL7165, where the converter knows the division (CommentEntryOf) and where CommentEntryResolver decides a carried candidate late (ConvertCommentEntryCandidate); the line is still discarded with the entry.

next.reason: 1985: "The comment-entry may be any combination of the characters from the computer's character set."; 2023: "No comment-entry paragraphs (AUTHOR, DATE-WRITTEN, etc.) remain; the identification division rules cover only PROGRAM-ID". The 1985 comment-entry belongs to the obsolete optional Identification Division paragraphs. No 2023 candidate covers comment-entries, so 2023 lacks the feature.
